newsitem.title: JAPAN: Boom in Japan PC sales may fall off.
newsitem.headline: Boom in Japan PC sales may fall off.

text.p: After expanding by a staggering 70 percent last year, Japan's PC market will probably grow by less than one-third in the current fiscal year due to slower home personal computer sales, industry officials said on Tuesday.
"The basic undertone is steady expansion, but the fact is things have shifted into cruising speed," said Mami Indo, analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research.
Some analysts revised downward their forecasts after a disappointing Christmas season and now expect slower personal computer sales for the year to the end of March.
Slower Christmas sales of home PCs after a cooling of the Windows 95 software fever from a year earlier, was mainly responsible for the deceleration, Indo said.

PC makers, which suffered from cut-throat price wars in 1995, are now focusing more on profits rather than sales, and decided late last year not to introduce cut-rate PCs aimed at individuals, other analysts said.
"It only reflects a change in their sales strategy," said Kazushi Shiga, analyst at Data Quest, adding that sales growth will boom again once makers start producing lower-cost models.
Japanese PC makers include Toshiba Corp, NEC Corp and Fujitsu Ltd.
Shiga expects growth of less than 30 percent for the Japanese PC market for the year to the end of March, down slightly from an earlier estimate.
Tetsuya Mizoguchi, the head of the Japan Electronic Industry Development Association's PC division, said a delay in the launch of new models has affected the sales trend.
A delay in the launch of PCs fitted with the new MMX chip made by Intel Corp has meant demand has not risen as quickly as expected, he said.
Such PCs were expected to appear on the market in the third quarter, but their introduction was delayed until January.
Shortages of new liquid-crystal displays and longer-life batteries also put restraints on sales of laptop and notebook computers, he said.
Mizoguchi said domestic PC sales may fall short of the association's target of 7.5 million units in the fiscal year which ends in March.
He added, however, that Japan would easily clear the 1996/97 shipment target in terms of value of 1.6 trillion yen ($13.1 billion) because of higher prices.
For the fiscal year starting from April, the association said it was keeping its shipment target unchanged at 9.3 million units.
"We expect some favourable factors to support sales next year, such as the introduction of Windows NT 4.0 software," Mizoguchi said.
